metadata.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

problem_summary.summary: Return the minimum value from a rotated ascending array containing unique integers.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a nonempty ascending array rotated from its sorted order. Return its minimum value.
constraints: nums was sorted and rotated between 1 and n times
The required algorithm runs in O(log n) time

brute_force.explanation: Scan the array while maintaining the smallest value seen so far.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every array element is considered, so the maintained minimum after the final element is the minimum of the entire array, independent of its rotation point.

optimized.explanation: Compare nums[mid] with nums[right]. If nums[mid] is greater, the minimum must be to the right of mid; otherwise the minimum is at mid or to its left. Keep mid in the second case because it may be the minimum.
optimized.correctness_idea: The right endpoint lies in the same sorted run as the minimum candidate when nums[mid] <= nums[right], so the minimum is in [left, mid]. When nums[mid] > nums[right], the rotation drop and minimum are strictly to mid's right. The invariant leaves the minimum in the interval until one index remains.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log n), where n is nums.length.

steps.event: Compare the middle with the right endpoint in [0, 6].
steps.condition: 1 <= 4, so the minimum is at mid or to its left.
6 > 1, so the minimum must be strictly right of mid.
7 > 1, so discard index 2 and everything to its left.
steps.action: Set left to 3; the interval now contains one value.

edge_cases.handling: The initial interval already contains one index, which is returned.
Comparisons repeatedly move the right endpoint toward index 0.

edge_cases.case: Minimum is at the final index
edge_cases.handling: A rotation by n - 1 positions can place the minimum last; comparisons narrow the interval to that index.
When the first value is the minimum, comparisons repeatedly move the right endpoint left until index 0 remains.
